requirement:
Node-insertion methods queue selections. They resolve no contents or edges,
render no inputs, and record no observations while building.

Awaiting with a configured agent resolves these selections in call order:

| Insertion | Contents delivered |
| --- | --- |
| `contents_of_current_node()` | The node identified by `ValidationContext::node_id`. |
| `contents_of_successors(label)` | Targets of edges whose labels equal `label`, in returned edge order, including duplicate targets. |

Each successful successor selection records its source, label, and target-set
fingerprint, even when nothing matches. Only selected targets have their contents
resolved. Each delivered node is recorded with its supplied snapshot's
fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.author_procedure`.
Input-resolution failures return `ValidationError::Graph`.
rationale:
I judged the three marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs` against each obligation in `node_contents`. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied test code was enough to map each obligation to an assertion. Together the tests cover every obligation.

- **Queue only while building.**
  - `dropped_builders_and_missing_agents_do_not_resolve_queued_inputs` drops a builder that queued `contents_of_current_node` and `contents_of_successors`. It asserts that `ctx.dependencies()` is empty. It sets `fail_edges`, so any resolution would error or be visible.
  - The same test awaits a builder with no agent and expects `NoAgentConfigured`. It then asserts that `state.reads` and `state.selections` are empty, so nothing was resolved without an agent.
  - `queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation` drops a builder and asserts that the agent received no requests.
- **Call order and current node.** `explicit_insertions_preserve_order_repetition_and_selection_snapshots` queues current, then successors(7), then current again. It asserts that the delivered contents are `[1, 3, 2, 3, 1]`, and that `state.reads` is `[1, 3, 2, 3, 1]`. This shows the node from `node_id` is delivered, and in call order.
- **Successor selection.**
  - The edges are `[(7,3),(8,99),(7,2),(7,3)]`. The test delivers only the label-7 targets, in returned edge order, with the duplicate target 3 kept (3, 2, 3). The label-8 target 99 is never read, which shows that only selected targets have their contents resolved.
- **Recorded selection and node dependencies.**
  - The same test asserts the trace. It contains `OutgoingEdges(1, 7, fingerprint of {2,3})`, which holds the source, label and target-set fingerprint. It also contains `Node(1|3|2, fp(content))` for each delivered node. Together these show the node fingerprints are recorded.
  - In `queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation`, edges `[]` and `[(8,99)]` give no match for label 7. The test asserts that no reads happen. It also asserts that the trace is exactly one `OutgoingEdges(1, 7, fingerprint of [])`, so an empty selection is still recorded.
- **Failures return `ValidationError::Graph`.**
  - The queued-reads test covers three failures. A read failure gives `Graph("read")`. An edge-listing failure gives `Graph("edges")`. A render-preparation failure gives `Graph("render")`.
  - After the render failure it asserts that the dependency trace is empty and that the agent was not invoked.

I found no required scenario that the tests miss. Three gaps are not required by the text, so I did not count them. The text does not require tests for a changing snapshot between repeated reads, for dependencies after a failed selection, or for a read failure on a successor target.

text: :::{req} judge.node_contents
Node-insertion methods queue selections. They resolve no contents or edges,
render no inputs, and record no observations while building.
Awaiting with a configured agent resolves these selections in call order:
| Insertion | Contents delivered |
| `contents_of_current_node()` | The node identified by `ValidationContext::node_id`. |
| `contents_of_successors(label)` | Targets of edges whose labels equal `label`, in returned edge order, including duplicate targets. |
Each successful successor selection records its source, label, and target-set
fingerprint, even when nothing matches. Only selected targets have their contents
resolved. Each delivered node is recorded with its supplied snapshot's
fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.author_procedure`.
Input-resolution failures return `ValidationError::Graph`.
:::{req} author_procedure
A `Criterion::execute` invocation receives one `Send + Sync`
`ValidationContext<'d, D>` for `D: Domain`, with tracked `inspection(&self)`
and the `ask(&self)` builder under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge`.
Each awaited ask builder runs its own conversation and returns its own submitted
answer. The context combines delivered node contents, tool reads, direct
inspection reads, and recorded edge selections into one dependency trace for
the criterion. It records the node identities and fingerprints of the supplied
contents. A later call that selects fewer nodes, or none, preserves earlier
inputs. An unawaited builder contributes no
agent-delivery dependencies.
Shared references support concurrent calls: builders, conversations, and
submission state remain independent, while updates to the trace are synchronized.
Calls can run concurrently without holding an exclusive context borrow across
an agent interaction or locking the whole context for the conversation.
The same context supports deterministic criteria under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures`.
